stories.headline: House GOP chairs ask Huang to brief on Megaspeed exec; Nvidia adds SE Asia chip tracking

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 5, House Foreign Affairs chair Brian Mast, China Select Committee chair John Moolenaar and Intelligence chair Rick Crawford released a letter asking Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for a joint, closed-door briefing on his interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom they call a publicly reported PRC intelligence asset, and on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign espionage.
key_facts.excerpt: sent a letter to NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang requesting that he appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on Huang's interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset, and NVIDIA's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.

key_facts.fact: The chairmen asked Huang to brief on Nov. 18 and to accept or offer an alternative date by Nov. 11; Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Nov. 17, the day before.
key_facts.excerpt: The lawmakers invited Huang to appear for an in-person joint briefing on Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings.

key_facts.fact: The request follows a New York Times report last week that US intelligence found Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, was funneling information to Beijing and had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York Times reported last week that U.S. intelligence found Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen determined to be funneling information to Beijing, had "developed a close relationship" with Jensen Huang.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia did not say whether Huang would attend and said regional cloud customers get only ordinary business information, adding that meeting customers is part of a CEO's job.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets—and zero information relevant to national security," the spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed is a Singapore-based buyer of Nvidia AI chips that US authorities have scrutinized on suspicion it helped Beijing gain access to chips barred from shipment to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Singpore-based company Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia. US authorities have scrutinized Megaspeed over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 6 that Nvidia now requires Southeast Asian customers to enroll in its fleet intelligence system, which tracks accelerator locations, to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker now requires customers in the region to enrol in its so-called fleet intelligence system — which tracks the location of AI accelerators owned by participating companies, among other metrics — in order to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners, or NCPs

key_facts.fact: Fleet intelligence remains voluntary and does not by default require sharing location data with Nvidia or the US government; Nvidia declined to say whether existing partners such as Megaspeed must sign up or whether the rule will extend beyond Southeast Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: fleet intelligence does not by default require participants to share location data with Nvidia or the US government... Nvidia declined to comment on this question or answer others for this story, including whether the new NCP requirement would be applied in regions beyond Southeast Asia.

stories.headline: Reuters: 600,000 Nvidia H200s sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds large-scale import approval

key_facts.fact: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China, two people told Reuters, in a stockpile whose size had not been reported before.
key_facts.excerpt: Stocks of nearly 600,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips have been stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China, according to a Reuters report... The stockpile of H200 chips, which had not been reported earlier

key_facts.fact: Beijing has allowed some shipments but no large-volume imports: several big Chinese internet firms each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months, and small quantities arrived via intermediaries.
key_facts.excerpt: Several Chinese companies received shipments of 10,000 H200 chips in the past few months... There have also been reports of chips being shipped through intermediaries and indirect routes.

key_facts.fact: An eight-card H200 server was offered in mainland China for more than 6 million yuan ($900,000) by end-October, about three times its price a year earlier; servers with Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips, barred from sale to China, were offered for more than 20 million yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: By the end of October, a server with eight H200 chips was being offered there for more than 6m yuan, about three times its price a year earlier. Servers with Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips, which the US does not allow to be sold to China, were offered for more than 20m yuan each.

key_facts.fact: Beijing wants Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to prefer Chinese chips, especially for inference, and total foreign-chip approvals could end up below 200,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing wants firms such as Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips instead... the total number of foreign chips China approves could end up below 200,000, Reuters reported.

key_facts.fact: Computing estimates the stranded chips are worth around $20 billion at typical prices of $32,000 to $40,000 each.
key_facts.excerpt: The high-end AI chips, which typically sell for $32,000-$ 40,000 a piece, are worth around $20 billion in total

key_facts.fact: In its latest quarterly filing, Nvidia said H200 sales to China were under 1% of data center revenue and took a $400 million charge for unsold H200 stock and purchase commitments.
key_facts.excerpt: In its latest quarterly filing, Nvidia said H200 sales to China came to less than 1% of its data centre revenue. It also took a $400m charge for unsold H200 stock and purchase commitments.

key_facts.fact: Separately, on Nov. 5 the US Commerce Department's BIS released a final rule extending the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' through Jan. 10, 2027; the rule would extend Entity List restrictions to foreign firms 50% or more owned by listed parties and was due to return on Nov. 10.
key_facts.excerpt: on November 5, 2026, the US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security ("BIS") released a final rule formally extending the suspension of the "Affiliates Rule" through January 10, 2027... The Affiliates Rule was set to come back into effect on November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: Microsoft tightens oversight of neocloud projects, debates signing new deals

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is tightening oversight of some data center projects from Nebius, IREN and Nscale, stepping away from those it deems risky and debating internally whether to sign new neocloud deals, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 5.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft is stepping away from projects it deems risky and debating internally whether to ink new neocloud deals, sources told Bloomberg.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg says some key Microsoft leaders have 'buyer's remorse' after signing tens of billions of dollars in contracts with neoclouds, which now face delays, regulatory snags and high costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Now, as neocloud companies grapple with delays, regulatory snags and high costs, some key Microsoft leaders have developed a case of buyer's remorse.

key_facts.fact: Some of the issues center on cabling at IREN's Texas site; IREN and Microsoft met last week and negotiated a revised timeline that may push completion back by several weeks or months.
key_facts.excerpt: Some of Microsoft's capacity issues center around the cabling at a site in Texas being developed by Iren... negotiated a revised timeline that may push back the site's completion by several weeks or months

key_facts.fact: After the report, IREN shares were down 18% to $17.83 and Nebius down 17% to $116.99.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Iren are down 18% to $17.83 following the story while Nebius is down 17% to $116.99.

key_facts.fact: In earnings on Nov. 5, IREN moved its target of more than $4 billion in annualized run-rate revenue from end-2026 to January 2027, with a possible extension to the end of February.
key_facts.excerpt: In its earnings announcement, IREN revised its target for reaching more than $4 billion in annualised run-rate revenue from the end of 2026 to January 2027, with a possible extension to the end of February.

key_facts.fact: A Microsoft spokesperson said adjusting plans according to circumstances is normal when managing large infrastructure projects; IREN declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: A Microsoft spokesperson said that adjusting plans according to circumstances is normal practice in managing large infrastructure projects; IREN declined to comment.

key_facts.fact: On its earlier fiscal first-quarter call, Microsoft reported capex of $45.2 billion for the September quarter, and CFO Amy Hood said some expected third-party capacity deliveries had been delayed.
key_facts.excerpt: "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," CFO Amy Hood said during the earnings call

stories.headline: Google commits $17B to first Wyoming data center, with 702 MW of fuel cells and carbon capture

key_facts.fact: Google announced on Nov. 5 a long-term $17 billion investment in its first Wyoming data center, in Laramie County, with Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power (AEP) and Related Digital.
key_facts.excerpt: we are announcing our first data center in the state of Wyoming, in partnership with Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power (AEP), and Related Digital. Google is making a long-term, $17 billion investment

key_facts.fact: The project is contracted with AEP for a 702 MW natural-gas fuel cell development with carbon capture and storage, using Bloom Energy cells; Google calls it the largest planned of its kind, and it takes Google's contracted carbon capture capacity to nearly 1 GW.
key_facts.excerpt: a first-of-its-kind, commercial-scale, 702 MW fuel cell development with carbon capture and storage (CCS) — the largest planned development of its kind to date... brings our total contracted CCS capacity to nearly 1 gigawatt.

key_facts.fact: Google says it will pay for 100% of the power it uses and cover infrastructure needs driven by its growth; the site will be air-cooled to limit water use.
key_facts.excerpt: We will pay for 100% of the power we use, and when we build data centers, we'll cover the infrastructure needs directly driven by our growth... our Wyoming data center will be air-cooled

key_facts.fact: Google and partners including Bloom are forming a Community Council after a Cheyenne meeting with more than 200 residents raised concerns about how data center growth is affecting the city.
key_facts.excerpt: Google, Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, Related Digital, AEP, and Bloom Energy are standing up a Community Council designed to develop common-sense solutions to support Cheyenne through this phase of growth.

key_facts.fact: Google says carbon capture will remove 'a large majority' of the plant's emissions but has not given a figure; the plant should be fully running by the end of 2028 and AEP said in October it would spend about $4 billion on it.
key_facts.excerpt: AEP said in October it would spend about $4B on the Bloom Energy plant near Cheyenne... the plant should be fully running by the end of 2028... Google says this will remove "a large majority" of the plant's emissions, but has not given a figure.

key_facts.fact: Reuters framed the move as pushing ahead as resistance grows after the midterms: of 41 data center ballot measures voted on this week, all but one went against data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: pushing ahead with a major AI infrastructure investment as political resistance to data center expansion grows following the US midterm elections. Of the 41 data center-related ballot measures voted on this week, all but one went against data

stories.headline: The Information: Nvidia pitches Apollo on turning old phone buildings into small AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has approached Apollo Global Management about a network of small AI data centers spanning as many as 20 US states, built in more than 130 buildings of Apollo-backed Brightspeed, a broadband provider reportedly nearing bankruptcy, The Information reported on Nov. 5.
key_facts.excerpt: the chipmaker has approached private equity firm Apollo Global Management (APO) about establishing a network of such facilities that could span as many as 20 U.S. states. The effort centers on buildings owned by Brightspeed, an Apollo-backed broadband provider that is reportedly nearing bankruptcy and operates more than 130 sites

key_facts.fact: The buildings total roughly 1 GW of available power, which could support tens of billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin servers.
key_facts.excerpt: the portfolio totaling roughly 1 gigawatt of available power... That capacity could support tens of billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin servers.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia sent Brightspeed a written proposal on Nov. 4 and requested data and site visits; staff discussed with suppliers possibly starting retrofits with Vera Rubin racks in Q1 2027, which is not a confirmed start.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia submitted a written proposal to Brightspeed on Wednesday and has requested additional data plus site visits. Nvidia staff has also discussed with suppliers the possibility of beginning building retrofits with Vera Rubin racks in the first quarter of 2027

key_facts.fact: Nvidia describes the sites as an 'inference network' for running trained models; it is unclear who would buy or lease the chips or how many buildings it wants to retrofit.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has described the proposed sites as an "inference network"... It remains unclear who would ultimately purchase or lease the chips... it is unclear how many Brightspeed buildings Nvidia wants to retrofit.

key_facts.fact: Retrofits would still need local permits for upgrades such as specialized cooling, but fewer approvals than ground-up construction.
key_facts.excerpt: Retrofitting existing structures would still need local permits for upgrades such as specialized cooling, but fewer approvals than ground-up construction

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Nov. 6 that about 40% of pending US data center capacity is in states whose newly elected governors promised to stop or pause construction, per Cleanview, on top of 46 local ballot measures approved or on track to pass.
key_facts.excerpt: about 40% of pending data center capacity in the US is planned to be built in states where newly elected governors have promised to stop or pause such construction, according to data from Cleanview... That's on top of 46 local ballot measures approved or on track to pass

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg Intelligence's Mandeep Singh estimates the results could shrink the $1.4 trillion of expected 2027 AI infrastructure spending by about 5% to 7%, with as much as 10 GW failing to come online next year as planned.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuesday's results stand to shrink the $1.4 trillion that technology companies were expected to spend on AI infrastructure by roughly 5% to 7% in 2027... as many as 10 gigawatts of data center capacity failing to come online next year as planned, Singh said.

stories.headline: Musk: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk posted on Nov. 6 that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production

key_facts.fact: Musk did not say whether production would move elsewhere, but Austin is the only known plant equipped to make the truck's specialized components.
key_facts.excerpt: The production plant in Austin, Texas, is the only Tesla facility that's known to assemble the Cybertruck, and that's equipped to make the specialized components required to build the vehicles. Musk hasn't mentioned if Cybertruck production will be moved elsewhere

key_facts.fact: Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill wrote that the truck 'lives on through Cybercab', and Musk replied 'True' to a user calling it Tesla's best vehicle, adding the fleet 'will be around for a long time'.
key_facts.excerpt: writing on X: "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."... Musk responded to the user with the word "true", adding: "But the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time."

key_facts.fact: Tesla sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, per Kelley Blue Book, against Musk's pre-launch prediction of 250,000 a year.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Before the pickup truck launched, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.

key_facts.fact: The Cybercab has no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors; Tesla began paid rides in a small Austin fleet in September, and US auto safety regulators are still asking whether it properly self-certified the vehicle.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. However, the automaker still has to answer the US auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab

stories.headline: Reuters: YMTC aims for up to 70% Chinese equipment at fourth flash memory factory in Wuhan

key_facts.fact: China's Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), its largest flash memory maker, targets at least 60% and as much as 70% domestic equipment at a planned fourth factory, up from just over half at its third, which starts operating later this year, two people told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: The target is at least 60% with an ambition of 70%, up from just over half at YMTC's third factory, which is due to begin operating later this year.

key_facts.fact: The Wuhan plant is expected to make YMTC's most advanced NAND chips, with more than 300 layers, mainly for data centers and AI applications.
key_facts.excerpt: The planned fourth factory in Wuhan... is expected to produce the company's most advanced NAND chips, featuring more than 300 layers of memory cells stacked vertically... focus mainly on storage chips for data centers and artificial intelligence applications.

key_facts.fact: Construction is expected to begin next year; YMTC has held only preliminary supplier talks and placed no formal orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Construction is expected to begin next year. The company has so far only held preliminary discussions with suppliers and has not placed formal orders.

key_facts.fact: Most added domestic orders should come from cleaning, polishing and etching; YMTC still relies on overseas suppliers for some sophisticated tools, including lithography and inspection.
key_facts.excerpt: Most of the additional domestic orders are expected to come from cleaning, polishing and etching stages of production... YMTC remains reliant on overseas suppliers for some sophisticated tools, including lithography and inspection.

key_facts.fact: YMTC has been on the US Entity List since December 2022, which requires US suppliers to get licenses to sell it certain technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Commerce Department added YMTC to its Entity List in December 2022, imposing licensing requirements on US suppliers seeking to sell certain technology to the company.

key_facts.fact: YMTC's NAND share in China rose to 38.5% in Q2 from 28% in 2025, overtaking Samsung as the country's top NAND maker, per Omdia; its third, fourth and fifth factories are each expected to process about 100,000 wafers a month when fully operational.
key_facts.excerpt: YMTC's NAND market share in China rose to 38.5% in the second quarter from 28% in 2025, overtaking Samsung as the top NAND maker in the country, according to data from Omdia. When fully operational, the third, fourth and fifth factories are each expected to process about 100,000 silicon wafers a month
